title: The first editor window after launch opens as quickly as the ones after it
goal: Opening the first capture or recording after the app starts takes about a fifth of a second longer than opening the next one, because the editor window is built from nothing the first time. Make the first window as quick as later ones, so opening a recording right after recording it feels instant even when it is the first thing opened.
notes: Found on 2026-10-02 while making a recording open at Stop (a-recording-has-its-thumbnail-and-opens-the-mome). Reproduce: remove the first step (openSampleRecording) from Scripts/playtest/a-recording-opens-at-stop-walk.json and run it with Scripts/playtest.sh --no-build: step 1 fails 'the window showed the picture 448 ms after Stop' (468, 547, 553 ms on reruns); with the step in it reads 107-188 ms. Timestamps written from AppCoordinator.openWindow, ImageEditorRootView.body and EditorView.body on a cold run: openWindowAction called at +60 ms after Stop, first root body +109 ms, first EditorView body +131 ms, then nothing until a SECOND EditorState() is made and the root body runs again at +326 ms (about 195 ms inside SwiftUI's first build of EditorView's subtree), root .task +341 ms, openWindow returns +388 ms. A warm run: openWindow asked +40, returned +81, picture +107. setActivationPolicy(.regular) and AppFront.activate took about 2 ms, so they are not it. Note SwiftUI builds EditorState twice on the first window (two 'state init' marks). The editor's code after .task is 2 ms; the cost is the view tree's first build (type metadata, symbol images, fonts, first CI/Metal contexts are candidates; `sample` on the probe attached too late to catch it, so profile with signposts or Instruments).
acceptance: The first editor window of a run shows its picture within 100 ms of the second window's time, measured the same way on the same machine
Measured with the open-at-stop walk run without its warm-up step, before and after, and the numbers are in the task log
No window, panel or Dock icon appears that the person did not ask for

log.note: Triage 2026-10-03: the same first-time-per-launch cost shows up in three other audits from the last day, so whoever takes this should look for one shared warm-up rather than four fixes: the first panel section fold after launch costs about 25ms (2026-10-02-section-fold-motion), the first key in the history strip about 25ms (2026-10-02-history-strip-arrow-keys, put down to macOS checking the menu bar), and the first recording after launch spends about 0.4s getting ready while the Record card is up (2026-10-03-recording-starts-on-enter). Only the window is in this task's acceptance; the others are context.

Reproduced: cold open-at-stop walk (warm-up step removed) read 614, 438, 608 ms; with the warm-up step 175, 161, 191 ms. Time Profiler (xctrace attached to the probe during the 3s recording): ~200 of 338 main-thread ms in swift_getTypeByMangledName under SwiftUI's first build of EditorView's tree. Fix: EditorWarmUp builds EditorView at launch in a window never ordered in, empty then holding a stand-in recording, and throws it away. Offscreen hosting view alone (no window, empty editor) only got to 364-390; blank video doc 172-300; a recording doc alone made it worse (the empty-editor first build came back) so it builds both states in order.

Final, eight alternating runs each, Stop to picture: cold first window 185,298,177,325,188,285,174,295 (mean 241); warm, beside an open window 179,176,163,179,164,160,149,170 (mean 167); second window after closing the first 316,277,297,180,325,159,295,280 (mean 266). Cold is within 100 ms of warm on mean and median, and no slower than a window reopened from zero. Checked during a walk: warm-up window never visible, activation policy stayed accessory (no Dock icon), probe had no on-screen windows 1.5s after launch, throwaway EditorState freed. Scripts/test.sh: 11042 tests pass. Walks green: a-recording-opens-at-stop, blank-canvas, a-recording-is-a-document, a-guide-recording-opens-sharp, redline.

left rough: a window opened while no other editor window is open costs ~100 ms more than one beside an open window (bimodal ~180 vs ~290 ms). sample(1) shows the main thread blocked in -[NSWindow _windowMoved:] -> displaysWillChange -> SLSIsDisplayChangedSeedValid and a first MenuBarInstance built from a Dock callback: the accessory -> regular switch. Same for any window opened from zero, not launch-specific, and mostly under the 300 ms budget, so not filed; file it if it shows up again. Also: SwiftUI restores the group's saved frame for the first window (_setFrameAutosaveName), a synchronous layout inside openWindow; removing the saved frame did not change the numbers.

EditorWarmUp (Sources/Photonz/EditorWarmUp.swift) builds the editor at launch in a never-shown window, empty then holding a stand-in recording. First window after launch, Stop to picture: 438-614 ms before, 174-325 (mean 241) now, against 149-179 (mean 167) beside an open window, so within 100 ms on mean and median. No window, panel or Dock icon (checked during a walk). Tests 11042 pass; open-at-stop and four other walks green. Audit 2026-10-03-first-window-quick. Commit 35ca3f31.
